title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 'Teichmülleries' study of maps (cartes, i.e. dessins) on surfaces. Here the map is the 'cyclotomic map' X_n, the regular n-gon drawn on the Riemann sphere Σ_P, with automorphism group D_P (dihedral of order 2n), and extended by an orientation-reversing involution τ. In the notation of the previous pages, Π_P^D is the 'fundamental group' attached to the D_P-action on Σ*_P, where Σ*_P is Σ_P minus the vertices. From p.84 it has the presentation <ρ, σ_{a0} | ρ^n = σ_{a0}^2 = 1>. Adding the orientation-reversing generator σ~_{a0} gives the presentation (86) of Π_P^{D,τ}: <ρ, σ, σ~ | ρ^n = σ^2 = σ~^2 = (σσ~)^2 = 1, σ~ρσ~ = ρ^{-1}>.

(87)-(88) restate this as an amalgamated free product D(ρ) *_{D_1} D(σ).
- D(ρ) = <ρ> ⋊ <σ~> is the dihedral group of order 2n (Grothendieck's 'diédral d'indice n').
- D(σ) = <σ> × <σ~> is the Klein four group ('diédral d'indice 2').
- The amalgamation is over D_1 = <σ~> ≅ Z/2.
This is the standard decomposition of the extended triangle group of signature (∞,2,n) generated by reflections. For n=3 it is the classical PGL_2(Z) ≅ S_3 *_{Z/2} V_4.

(89) re-expresses (77). Π_P^D ≅ Π_{0,3}/<ρ_1^2, ρ_∞^n>. This is the orbifold fundamental group of P^1(C) with signature ∞·(0) + 2·(1) + n·(∞), i.e. the free product Z/2 * Z/n; for n=3 it is PSL_2(Z). The identification sends (ρ, σ_{a0}) to (ρ_∞, ρ_1).

Grothendieck then proposes an 'a priori' route to (89). Take the quotient of Σ_P by the faithful D_P-action. It is a complex algebraic curve of genus 0, branched at three kinds of points:
- the vertices R_s, with ramification 2 (the vertices of X_n have valence 2);
- the edge midpoints Q_a, with ramification 2;
- the face centres P_ω, with ramification n.
The quotient is identified with P^1_C, uniquely once normalised by (90): R_s→0, Q_a→1, P_ω→∞. Removing the vertices gives the orbifold group above.

The margin note flags this as 'un peu une tricherie' (a bit of a cheat). One would first need to know that the map on Σ_P is the pullback of the universal map {0}⊂[0,1]⊂P^1 under a well-determined morphism Σ_P→P^1_C. The text starts to say exactly that and then turns to the pinned (épinglé) case. The next page makes it explicit: z ↦ −(z^n−1)^2/(4z^n), which is a Galois D_n-cover branched over 0,1,∞ with indices 2,2,n.
errors: Notation slips: σ_a is used where σ_{a0} is meant (and σ~_a for σ~_{a0}). 'Groupe diédral d'indice n' means dihedral of order 2n, and 'd'indice 2' means the Klein four group. Not mathematical errors.

The margin note itself admits a circularity: using the quotient Σ_P/D_P ≅ P^1 to justify (89) presupposes that the map is the pullback of the universal map. Grothendieck flags this rather than resolving it on this page.

ideas.what: Extended (orientation-reversing) group of the regular n-gon map written as an amalgam D_n *_{Z/2} (Z/2×Z/2).
ideas.modern_name: Extended triangle group (∞,2,n)* as an amalgamated free product (for n=3, PGL_2(Z) ≅ S_3 *_{Z/2} V_4).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein–Fricke; Serre's Trees for the PGL_2(Z) case; Jones–Singerman theory of maps).
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartographic groups in general, not this specific amalgam.

ideas.what: Π_P^D ≅ π_1^orb(P^1; ∞,2,n) = Z/2 * Z/n, identifying the generators of the map's group with loops around 1 and ∞.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group / Fuchsian triangle group with a cusp; the oriented cartographic group quotient.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; in the dessins setting Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984), Jones–Singerman 1978.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, triangle groups, maps as finite sets with group action).

ideas.what: Recovering the map as the quotient of the surface by its automorphism group, normalised so that vertices→0, edge midpoints→1, face centres→∞ (Belyi-type function).
ideas.modern_name: Regular dessin as a Galois Belyi cover; quotient map Σ → Σ/Aut ≅ P^1.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard working-out of the group of the regular n-gon dessin and its extended group as an orbifold and amalgamated triangle group, plus the standard Belyi-quotient normalisation. The self-critical margin note about circularity is a nice glimpse of method but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'ce qui s'écrit aussi' matches the image (the leading 'ce' is barely legible).
In (88), the struck-through text after D^+·{1,σ~_a} looks like '·D(σ_a)', and 'engendré' is crossed out and replaced by 'défini'. The small note under D^+ reads roughly 'engendré par ρ, avec ρ^n=1'.

Margin note at bottom left is only partly legible. It reads approximately: 'C'est un peu une tricherie, car pour cette construction, il faut d'abord établir que ... qui ici n'est plus ... il faudrait un isomorphisme Σ_P→P^1_C, cf. plus bas'.
'Il est clair [?] que la carte...' is uncertain; the opening words could equally be '... dire que la carte envisagée sur Σ_P est l'image inverse de la carte universelle'.
The words added above 'isomorphe' read 'une courbe alg. complexe', as transcribed.
